newsitem.title: USA: Catastrophe Exchange to announce new subscribers.
newsitem.headline: Catastrophe Exchange to announce new subscribers.

text.p: The Catastrophe Risk Exchange, which opened for business on Tuesday, plans to announce next week that it has signed on several new subscribers, an exchange official said.
"Catex," which allows customers to trade insurance risks, currently has one subscriber, Everest Reinsurance Holdings Inc.
But next week, Catex will be "announcing a number of other subscribers," said Catex vice president Frank Fortunato.
The exchange is currently scheduling the installation of its system at a number of subscribers, he said.
"We're seeing a significant amount of interest from the industry. We're very pleased with the progress we're seeing," he said.
Catex would allow subscribers to swap catastrophic risk exposures over a nationwide computer system.

The system would allow an insurer to reduce its exposure to catastrophes by allowing it to pay another company to accept some of its risk or by allowing it to give away one set of risks in return for accepting a separate bundle of risks.
The exchange is one of a number of new mechanisms being developed to help insurers reduce the risk of massive losses from a major catastrophe.
